unit.why: A moral teaching on guarding one's speech is illustrated by one narrative: R. Yitzhak of Drohobych fails to fall asleep, discovers his sin of silent complicity in mockery of the Besht, travels to Medzhybizh, and the Besht recognizes and forgives him.
unit.boundary_note: Division opens as item ד of the alphabetical section on mockery (מענין ליצנות) and ends with the heading for the next section (מענין מאכלים).

stories.start_quote: כמו שאירע להק׳ רבינו יצחק מדראהביטש
stories.summary_en: R. Yitzhak of Drohobych, whose inability to sleep after reciting 'Into Your hand' signaled an unrepented sin, realizes he stood silently while scoffers mocked the Besht; he rides at once to Medzhybizh, prays unknown in the Besht's study hall, and the Besht calls him by name at the Torah reading, names his offense and forgives him wholeheartedly.

tags.why: Narrative is wrapped in a homiletic frame warning against evil speech, closing with an admonition to the reader.

quotes: קרא אותו מרן מורה מרינו ר׳ יצחק בן ר׳ יוסף
התלוצץ על הבעש״ט ונסע דרך כזה
tags.why: The Besht knows the stranger's name and his sin without being told.

quotes: ואינם רוצין לקבלו עד שיעשה תשובה
tags.why: Heaven signals refusal through his inability to sleep.

quotes: ואינם רוצין לקבלו עד שיעשה תשובה
ונסע תיכף לק״ק מעזיבז לבקש ממנו מטו
tags.why: He seeks out his sin and travels to ask forgiveness.
The prohibition against evil speech and mockery, and failing to protest, is at issue.

quotes: ואם אירע שלא יכול לישן היה יודע שעשה איזה חטא
tags.why: Sleeplessness functions as a heavenly sign or sanction for sin.

quotes: ונסע תיכף לק״ק מעזיבז לבקש ממנו מטו
tags.why: He journeys to the Besht's town to see him.

quotes: שתיכף שיאמר בידך אפקיד ישן לו
tags.why: He recites the bedtime prayer and prays in the study hall.

quotes: והלך הרב ר׳ יצחק לבית מדרשו של מרן להתפלל
tags.why: The recognition scene takes place in the Besht's study hall.

quotes: שהי׳ עומד במסיבות לצים שעשו ליצנות ממרן
tags.why: He was among people who scoffed at the Besht, i.e. outside or opposed to his circle.
A man complicit in mocking the Besht comes to him and is reconciled.
The Besht's wholehearted forgiveness is shown as a virtue.

missing_concepts: lashon hara / mockery of a tzaddik
sleep as a sign of heavenly acceptance
